title: Time Zones and the Calendar
summary: Why it is morning in India while it is night in America, and how calendars work.

steps.title: Earth turns
sentences: The Earth spins once in about 24 hours.
At any moment half the world faces the Sun and has daytime, and the other half has night.
That is why people far apart have different times.

steps.title: Time zones
sentences: The world is divided into time zones, roughly 15 degrees of longitude wide, one hour apart.
India uses one time zone for the whole country, Indian Standard Time, which is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Universal Time.
Some big countries, like the United States, use several.

steps.title: The calendar
sentences: A year is the time Earth takes to go once around the Sun, about 365 and a quarter days.
We add an extra day, 29 February, every four years in a leap year to keep up.
A week of seven days and a month come from old ideas about the Moon and planets.

steps.title: Many calendars
sentences: Different cultures also use other calendars, such as the Tamil calendar with Chithirai as its first month, and the Hindu, Islamic and Chinese calendars.
Many are based on the Moon or the Sun.
That is why some festivals fall on different dates each year in the common calendar.

facts: Nepal's time is 5 hours 45 minutes ahead of UTC, a rare 45 minute offset.
The International Date Line is where the date changes as you cross the Pacific Ocean.
Tamil New Year usually falls in mid April.
